title: Fix docs/sync-conflict-resolution.md's LWW tie-break rule — it contradicts the implemented and tested behavior
rule: AG-8 (doc/code parity); FB-2/FB-3 (LWW ordering, clock-skew handling)

evidence.quote:
> strictly newer timestamp wins. If both timestamps are equal the remote row
> is silently dropped (the LWW rule is `remoteTimestamp > localTimestamp`).

// The one true tie (equal `updated_at`, no decisive server timestamp) is
    // resolved by preferring remote so two devices that wrote the same value
test('exactly identical timestamps, no synced_at → remote wins', () {

why: The canonical doc says ties are dropped in favor of local (strict `remoteTimestamp > localTimestamp`) and never mentions a clock-skew window. The actual implementation and its exhaustive, intentional test coverage do the opposite for the common case: outside a ±5s skew window ties do stay local, but *inside* the window — the realistic case for near-simultaneous writes from a user's own two devices — an exact tie goes to REMOTE (code comment: 'prefer remote... converge instead of bouncing'), and a `synced_at` server-timestamp tie-break exists that the doc never describes at all. An engineer implementing a new merger or debugging a 'my edit got overwritten' report will read the doc, get the tie-break backwards for the realistic case, and either mis-implement a new merger or chase a phantom bug.
recommendation: Rewrite the 'Push/pull invariant' section to describe the actual 3-tier rule in DriftMergeStore.remoteIsNewer: (1) outside ±5s skew, strict remote>local wins and ties stay local; (2) inside ±5s skew with both sides carrying synced_at, the server timestamp decides; (3) inside the window with no decisive synced_at, remote wins to force convergence. Point the doc at drift_merge_store.dart:113-152 so future changes are easy to diff against it.
acceptance_criteria: docs/sync-conflict-resolution.md's tie-break wording matches lib/core/sync/merge/drift_merge_store.dart:113-152 exactly, confirmed by re-reading both side by side
the doc states the ±5s clock-skew window and the synced_at tie-break, matching DriftMergeStore.clockSkewTieBreakWindow
